explanations.explanation: Three, baker. Verse 2 says Israel is to set apart three cities within the land the LORD is giving them. I can barely keep three cookie trays straight when the timer goes off, so I respect it. Small number, big job, and the next verses show what the job is.

Seven has a nice ring to it, friend, but the text says three. Israel is to set apart three cities within the land the LORD is giving them to possess. Seven would be a lot of extra bricks to haul around.
Twelve cities! I'd need a bigger bakery just to picture it. But the text says three, set apart within the land the LORD is giving Israel. Sometimes the smaller number is the one on the page.

explanations.answer: So any manslayer can flee to these cities
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. Verse 3 says to build roads and divide the land into three regions "so that any manslayer can flee to these cities." The roads are there so the cities can actually be reached. A refuge nobody can get to is just a nice view.

explanations.answer: So the Levites can collect offerings
explanations.explanation: I see where you're heading, friend, but this verse never mentions offerings. It says the roads and the three regions are so that any manslayer can flee to these cities. The whole point is getting to a safe place.

explanations.answer: So the tribes can trade their goods
explanations.explanation: Roads and trade do go together in my head too, friend. But the text says nothing about trading here. It says the land is divided into three regions so that any manslayer can flee to these cities.

explanations.answer: One who killed his neighbor by accident
explanations.explanation: Right on it, baker. Verse 4 says he killed his neighbor accidentally, without intending to harm him. That detail carries the whole teaching. Hold onto it, because the passage comes back to a very different kind of case.

explanations.answer: One who killed his neighbor in a quarrel
explanations.explanation: A quarrel isn't anywhere in this verse, friend. Verse 4 says the man killed his neighbor accidentally, without intending to harm him. That's the man who flees to one of these cities to save his life.

explanations.answer: One who killed his neighbor for revenge
explanations.explanation: Revenge is a different case, friend, and the passage gets to a man like that later, in verse 11. Here in verse 4, the manslayer killed his neighbor accidentally, without intending to harm him. Keep the two men apart in your head and the whole passage gets easier.

explanations.answer: The blade flies off the handle
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. Verse 5 says he swings his axe to chop down a tree, but the blade flies off the handle and strikes and kills his neighbor. It's a sad, sudden moment, and I think that's why the example sticks. It shows what accidentally really looks like.
Close to the picture, friend, but not what the verse says. Verse 5 says the blade flies off the handle. That's the part that strikes his neighbor.

explanations.answer: The tree falls the wrong way
explanations.explanation: That's a believable woodcutting mishap, friend, but the text doesn't say it. Verse 5 says the blade flies off the handle and strikes his neighbor. The tree isn't the problem in this example.

explanations.answer: The avenger of blood might chase him down
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. Verse 6 says the avenger of blood might pursue the manslayer in a rage and strike him dead. The city gives him somewhere to run to. Without one, the danger follows him down the road.

explanations.answer: The elders might sell him as a servant
explanations.explanation: Nothing about selling anyone shows up here, friend. Verse 6 names the danger: the avenger of blood might pursue the manslayer in a rage. That's why he needs a city to flee to.

explanations.answer: The priests might bar him from worship
explanations.explanation: The priests don't come up in this verse, friend. The danger in verse 6 is the avenger of blood, who might pursue the manslayer in a rage. That's what the city is there for.

I know it's a tricky one, friend, but the text says the opposite. Verse 6 says that if the avenger strikes him dead, it would be "though he did not deserve to die, since he did not intend any harm." The man didn't intend harm, so he doesn't deserve to die.

Right, baker. Verse 6 says the avenger might strike him dead "though he did not deserve to die, since he did not intend any harm." This man didn't mean it. That's why the passage gives him a place to run.
True, baker. Verse 9 says that if the LORD gives Israel all the land He promised, they are to add three more cities to these three. Six cities in all. That's a lot of roads.
Not quite, friend. Verse 9 says that if the LORD gives Israel all the land He promised, they are to add three more cities to these three. So the answer is True.

True, baker. Verse 9 says this comes "if you carefully keep all these commandments I am giving you today, loving the LORD your God and walking in His ways at all times." Then comes the command to add three more cities. The keeping and the loving are right there in the sentence.

It's actually True, friend. Verse 9 says the extra cities come if Israel carefully keeps all these commandments, loving the LORD their God and walking in His ways at all times. Those words are right there in the verse.

Innocent, baker. Verse 10 says "Thus innocent blood will not be shed in the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance." It also adds, "so that you will not be guilty of bloodshed." The cities are there to protect people who didn't deserve to die.
Royal blood sounds fancy, friend, but verse 10 doesn't say it. The word is innocent: innocent blood will not be shed in the land. That's what the cities are there to prevent.
I get why you'd think it, friend, but verse 10 says something else. The word there is innocent. The cities are about keeping innocent blood from being shed in the land the LORD is giving Israel.

explanations.answer: Bring him back to the avenger of blood
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. Verse 12 says the elders of his city must send for him, bring him back, and hand him over to the avenger of blood to die. This man killed out of hate, so the city doesn't shelter him. The refuge was for the man who didn't intend harm.

explanations.answer: Let him stay in that city
explanations.explanation: Not this man, friend. In verse 12 the elders of his own city must send for him and bring him back. Then they hand him over to the avenger of blood to die. A man who hated his neighbor and lay in wait doesn't get to hide there.

explanations.answer: Send him to stand before the priests
explanations.explanation: You're thinking of verse 17, friend, where a false witness case is brought before the priests and judges. That's a different situation. In verse 12 the elders must send for the man, bring him back, and hand him over to the avenger of blood to die.
Not this time, friend. Verse 13 says, "You must show him no pity." This is the man who hated his neighbor, lay in wait and killed him. So the answer is False.
Right, baker. Verse 13 says, "You must show him no pity." It also says Israel is to purge from Israel the guilt of shedding innocent blood. Mercy for the accidental case, no pity for the planned one.

Move, baker. Verse 14 says, "You must not move your neighbor's boundary marker." Those markers were set up by their ancestors to mark the inheritance. Sliding one over a few feet is the kind of sneaky thing I'd only try with a cookie on the cooling rack.
Repairing sounds helpful, friend, but verse 14 gives a different word. It says Israel must not move a neighbor's boundary marker. Their ancestors set those markers up to mark the inheritance.
Inspecting is harmless enough, friend, but that's not the word. Verse 14 says you must not move your neighbor's boundary marker. It was set up by their ancestors to mark the inheritance.
Two or three, baker. Verse 15 says a matter "must be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses." One lone voice isn't enough. It takes more than one person saying so.
That's more than the text asks for, friend. Verse 15 says a matter must be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses. A lone witness is not enough.
Ten or twelve would be a whole crowd, friend, and the verse asks for far fewer. Verse 15 says a matter must be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses. A lone witness isn't sufficient.

Not just the accused, friend. Verse 17 says both parties to the dispute must stand in the presence of the LORD, before the priests and judges who are in office at that time. Both sides stand there, so the answer is False.

That's right, baker. Verse 17 says both parties to the dispute must stand in the presence of the LORD. They stand before the priests and judges in office at that time. The accuser has to stand there too.
Yes, baker. Verse 18 says, "The judges shall investigate thoroughly." They don't just take someone's word for it. Thorough means checking, then checking again.
Casting lots isn't mentioned here, friend. Verse 18 says the judges shall investigate thoroughly. That's their job in this case.
A king doesn't come into this verse, friend. Verse 18 gives the work to the judges, and it says they shall investigate thoroughly.

explanations.answer: Do to him what he intended for his brother
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. Verse 19 says, "you must do to him as he intended to do to his brother." The liar gets what he planned for the man he accused. The text says this is how Israel purges the evil from among them.

explanations.answer: Make him pay a fine to the priests
explanations.explanation: A fine isn't in this verse, friend. Verse 19 says, "you must do to him as he intended to do to his brother." The priests are mentioned earlier in the case, but not as collecting money.

explanations.answer: Send him away to live in another town
explanations.explanation: Moving him to another town isn't what the text says, friend. Verse 19 says, "you must do to him as he intended to do to his brother." Whatever he planned for the man he accused is what comes back to him.
Afraid, baker. Verse 20 says, "Then the rest of the people will hear and be afraid." Word gets around. When people hear what happened to a liar, I think they'll think twice before trying it.
Proud isn't the word, friend. Verse 20 says the rest of the people will hear and be afraid. That fear is what the verse points to.
Grateful is a nice thought, friend, but the verse says something else. Verse 20 says the rest of the people will hear and be afraid.
True, baker. Verse 20 says the people "will never again do anything so evil among you." That's what Moses, Israel's leader, tells them will follow. The words are right there in the verse.
It's True, friend. Verse 20 says that after the rest of the people hear and are afraid, they "will never again do anything so evil among you." Those words are right there in the verse.
